label: T
paragraphXml: <w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" ns1:paraId="7DF5DFBA" ns1:textId="4482FABF" w:rsidR="00DB659A" w:rsidRPr="00363C34" w:rsidRDefault="00516EBF" w:rsidP="00DB659A"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t>T</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidR="00DB659A" w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t>.</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidR="00DB659A" w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:tab /><w:t>whereas on 16 July 2025, the Commission presented a set of proposals on the 2028-2034 MFF Regulation and the EU Own Resources Decision, followed by legislative proposals for the setting up of new EU programmes, funds and instruments;</w:t></w:r></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" ns1:paraId="2D7CE8D3" ns1:textId="1FDFB2C4" w:rsidR="00516EBF" w:rsidRPr="00363C34" w:rsidRDefault="00516EBF" w:rsidP="00516EBF"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /></w:pPr></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" ns1:paraId="13C4CC38" ns1:textId="5F3C492E" w:rsidR="00516EBF" w:rsidRPr="00363C34" w:rsidRDefault="00516EBF" w:rsidP="00516EBF"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t>1.</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:tab /><w:t>Underlines that the next MFF must equip the Union with the necessary financial means to respond to a rapidly evolving geopolitical, economic and social environment, while delivering on both long-standing policies and emerging priorities; insists that the EU budget must remain an investment budget capable of supporting citizens, regions and businesses, in particular SMEs, while strengthening the Union’s resilience, competitiveness and social cohesion;</w:t></w:r></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" ns1:paraId="19DB1462" ns1:textId="6863322E" w:rsidR="00516EBF" w:rsidRPr="00363C34" w:rsidRDefault="00516EBF" w:rsidP="00516EBF"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t>2.</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:tab /><w:t>Calls for the 2028</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidR="009D5108" w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t>-</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t>2034 MFF to be set at 1.27</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidR="009D5108" w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t> </w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t xml:space="preserve">% of EU </w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidR="009D5108" w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t>gross national income (</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t>GNI</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidR="009D5108" w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t>)</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t xml:space="preserve">, while the NGEU debt servicing </w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidR="009D5108" w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t>–</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t xml:space="preserve"> equivalent to an additional 0.11</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidR="009D5108" w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t> </w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t xml:space="preserve">% of </w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidR="0026393B" w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t xml:space="preserve">EU </w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t xml:space="preserve">GNI </w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidR="009D5108" w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t>–</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t xml:space="preserve"> should be excluded from the 1.27</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidR="009D5108" w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t> </w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t xml:space="preserve">% and accounted for over and above the ceilings; reiterates that the next MFF must be more ambitious in size, as the current level of financing does not match the Union’s political ambitions, and must be protected from inflationary shocks; stresses that this level constitutes the minimum necessary to enable the Union to deliver on its Treaty commitments, respond to citizens’ expectations, and address major challenges, including the return of large-scale warfare in the </w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidR="009D5108" w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t>EU’s</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t xml:space="preserve"> neighbourhood, evolving security threats, a highly challenging economic and social backdrop, a competitiveness gap and the worsening climate and biodiversity crises; </w:t></w:r></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" ns1:paraId="1F0FFE3D" ns1:textId="77777777" w:rsidR="00A72B8B" w:rsidRPr="00363C34" w:rsidRDefault="00A72B8B" w:rsidP="00A72B8B"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /><w:widowControl w:val="0" /></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t>40.</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:tab /><w:t>Recognises that all of the EU’s eastern border regions face heightened economic, social and security challenges due to Russia’s war of aggression against Ukraine and other geopolitical threats, including hybrid threats; stresses the need for comprehensive MFF support to strengthen their defence, preparedness, resilience and security, as well as their economic, social and territorial development; therefore calls for a comprehensive response across EU programmes and sustained EU level support, including financial assistance under the national plans;</w:t></w:r></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" ns1:paraId="43992DD2" ns1:textId="3652CC6A" w:rsidR="00A72B8B" w:rsidRPr="00363C34" w:rsidRDefault="00A72B8B" w:rsidP="00A72B8B"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /></w:pPr></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" ns1:paraId="667FABF3" ns1:textId="77777777" w:rsidR="00A72B8B" w:rsidRPr="00363C34" w:rsidRDefault="00A72B8B" w:rsidP="00A72B8B"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /><w:widowControl w:val="0" /><w:rPr><w:i /><w:iCs /></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:rPr><w:i /><w:iCs /></w:rPr><w:t>Heading 2</w:t></w:r></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" ns1:paraId="4AF4813D" ns1:textId="191D8C94" w:rsidR="00A72B8B" w:rsidRPr="00363C34" w:rsidRDefault="00A72B8B" w:rsidP="00A72B8B"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /><w:widowControl w:val="0" /></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:t>41.</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00363C34"><w:tab /><w:t xml:space="preserve">Welcomes the significant reinforcement of heading 2 on ‘Competitiveness, prosperity and security’, which is allocated EUR 522.2 billion in 2025 prices in the 2028-2034 MFF, representing 30 % of the total MFF compared to EUR 224.8 billion or 17 % in the current period; notes that this more than doubling of resources reflects the Union’s commitment to research, innovation, strategic autonomy, strategic industrial sectors and infrastructures, water resilience, emerging technologies, biotech, the green and digital transition, critical raw materials, energy security, space, defence, transport and military mobility, creative industries, education, culture, democracy and fundamental rights, economic and social resilience, technological sovereignty and support for SMEs, startups and scale-ups; acknowledges that this substantial increase responds to Parliament’s long-standing calls for greater investment in these areas and stresses that it should be implemented in a manner that ensures strategic coherence and maximises EU added-value; </w:t></w:r></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" w:rsidR="009A12A6" w:rsidRPr="00E6145F" w:rsidP="00075FB2" ns1:paraId="6F36EB89" ns1:textId="4A3B9905"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidRPr="00E6145F"><w:t>48.</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00E6145F"><w:tab /><w:t xml:space="preserve">Underlines that society-based independent fact-checking networks can play a role in detecting and combating disinformation campaigns and provide valuable insights for DSA risk assessments and mitigation; notes that independent fact-checking organisations need technical support and stable conditions in which to operate; considers that the European Network of Fact-Checkers, announced by the Commission in 2025, could serve as a valuable tool to achieve this; stresses that, to be credible and effective, fact-checking organisations must uphold strict standards of political neutrality, independence from online platform providers, and methodological objectivity; emphasises the importance of collaboration between fact-checkers, </w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00E6145F" w:rsidR="009212DA"><w:t>OSINT</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00E6145F"><w:t xml:space="preserve"> researchers, journalists, communicators and policymakers; further underlines the importance of supporting networks of fact-checkers in candidate and potential candidate countries;</w:t></w:r></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" w:rsidR="009A12A6" w:rsidRPr="00E6145F" w:rsidP="009A12A6" ns1:paraId="28F6CA93" ns1:textId="2966BF5F"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="Normal12a" /><w:rPr><w:bCs /><w:iCs /></w:rPr></w:pPr></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" w:rsidR="009A12A6" w:rsidRPr="00E6145F" w:rsidP="009A12A6" ns1:paraId="1EC64125" ns1:textId="77777777"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /><w:rPr><w:b /><w:bCs /><w:i /><w:iCs /></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidRPr="00E6145F"><w:rPr><w:b /><w:bCs /><w:i /><w:iCs /></w:rPr><w:t>Civil society, academia, culture and civic participation</w:t></w:r></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" w:rsidR="009A12A6" w:rsidRPr="00E6145F" w:rsidP="009A12A6" ns1:paraId="4C563622" ns1:textId="1D005290"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidRPr="00E6145F"><w:t>49.</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00E6145F"><w:tab /><w:t>Stresses the crucial role that active, vibrant and independent civil society plays as one of the core pillars in defending our democracy, not only in acting as a watchdog by exposing and actively combating malicious interference in democratic processes, but also in serving as a fundamental force in the long-term effort to build stronger and more resilient societies; underlines, in particular, the important role of civil society in upholding the values enshrined in Article</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00E6145F" w:rsidR="005E306D"><w:t> </w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="00E6145F"><w:t>2 TEU;</w:t></w:r></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" ns1:paraId="06785800" ns1:textId="49FEFA79" w:rsidR="00A93C27" w:rsidRPr="001B5B81" w:rsidRDefault="00A93C27" w:rsidP="00A93C27"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidRPr="001B5B81"><w:rPr><w:bCs /><w:iCs /></w:rPr><w:t>51.</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="001B5B81"><w:rPr><w:bCs /><w:iCs /></w:rPr><w:tab /><w:t>Recalls that Article 46 of the European Border and Coast Guard Agency Regulation</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="001B5B81"><w:rPr><w:rStyle w:val="FootnoteReference" /><w:bCs /><w:iCs /></w:rPr><w:footnoteReference w:id="48" /></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="001B5B81"><w:rPr><w:bCs /><w:iCs /></w:rPr><w:t xml:space="preserve"> can be activated in cases of potential violations of fundamental rights; calls on the agency to proactively make full use of all the tools at its disposal, in particular the possibility of activating Article 46 in cases of potential fundamental rights violations;</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="001B5B81"><w:t>52.</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="001B5B81"><w:tab /><w:t>Urges the Member States to take due account of the recommendations made by the Council of Europe Commissioner for Human Rights in his report entitled ‘Protecting the Defenders: Ending repression of human rights defenders assisting refugees, asylum seekers and migrants in Europe’</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="001B5B81"><w:rPr><w:vertAlign w:val="superscript" /></w:rPr><w:footnoteReference w:id="49" /></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="001B5B81"><w:t>; stresses the importance of maintaining public discourse grounded in respect for human dignity, while underlining the importance of a fact-based and responsible public debate on migration and asylum; strongly condemns recurrent anti-refugee and anti-migrant rhetoric;</w:t></w:r></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" ns1:paraId="51D4A1E2" ns1:textId="5CCB7414" w:rsidR="00A93C27" w:rsidRPr="001B5B81" w:rsidRDefault="00A93C27" w:rsidP="00A93C27"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /></w:pPr></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" ns1:paraId="6553498B" ns1:textId="77777777" w:rsidR="00A93C27" w:rsidRPr="001B5B81" w:rsidRDefault="00A93C27" w:rsidP="00A93C27"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /><w:rPr><w:b /><w:i /></w:rPr></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidRPr="001B5B81"><w:rPr><w:b /><w:i /></w:rPr><w:t>Gender-based violence, women’s rights and the rights of LGBTIQ+ people</w:t></w:r></w:p>

<w:p xmlns:ns1="http://schemas.microsoft.com/office/word/2010/wordml" xmlns:w="http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main" ns1:paraId="4BC6B411" ns1:textId="5C169FE9" w:rsidR="00A93C27" w:rsidRPr="001B5B81" w:rsidRDefault="00A93C27" w:rsidP="00A93C27"><w:pPr><w:pStyle w:val="NormalHanging12a" /></w:pPr><w:r w:rsidRPr="001B5B81"><w:t>53.</w:t></w:r><w:r w:rsidRPr="001B5B81"><w:tab /><w:t>Strongly condemns the backsliding on women’s and LGBTIQ+ rights in several Member States; calls on the Commission and the Member States to protect and promote gender equality and fundamental rights, including by addressing disinformation and organised campaigns that seek to limit these rights, and to take the necessary measures to promote gender representation;</w:t></w:r></w:p>
